name: KY-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican seats in the country
Comer holds a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising advantage with $1.6 million on hand versus under $8,000 for Williams
Prediction markets price Comer at about a 98 percent win probability
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending indicate the race is competitive
model.rationale: The R+23 fundamentals, Comer's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising position all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and no polling, ratings, or spending patterns suggest any crack in that advantage. Markets and the underlying numbers align on a margin of roughly 20 points.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Comer or a dramatic national wave against Republicans would meaningfully narrow a margin this wide.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's 1st District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent James Comer is seeking another term with every structural advantage that entails. He has raised about $2.3 million and holds roughly $1.6 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Drew Williams has raised about $223,000 with under $8,000 remaining. No outside groups have invested in the race, and no public polling or expert ratings flag it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Comer roughly a 98 percent chance of holding the seat. The district's R+23 lean, combined with incumbency and the lopsided fundraising gap, points to a margin in the neighborhood of 20 points. The forecast places this race firmly in the Safe Republican column, with the Democratic nominee needing an extraordinary and unforeseen shift to make it competitive.
